title: Historical typed MCP host and capability integration
summary: Implemented a Python MCP runtime with typed registration, dispatch, compatibility, approval and provenance before moving ownership to the product repository.

dates.note: Exact project start/end dates remain unknown. Direct local source/history review on 2026-10-29 supplements the supplied October 5 snapshot and separately dated owner statements. Commit milestones and review dates are not project starts or release dates.

facts.text: Implemented a typed Python MCP host with dynamic tool/resource/prompt registration, model-derived signatures, synchronous/asynchronous dispatch and explicit capability-pack entry points.
Added runtime compatibility checks, descriptor-controlled approval gates, UUID request traces and structured repository/commit/source provenance.
The shared host was later removed during product-ownership consolidation; the Configuration Engine pack was separately owned and its workflow bridge was a placeholder.

Adapted MCP SDK constructor differences and generated keyword signatures from Pydantic field definitions; routed synchronous/asynchronous handlers into trace records distinguishing success, blocked approval and execution failures.

notes: Historical implemented capability, not evidence that this shared host is the current deployment architecture.
Do not infer authorship of the separately owned Configuration Engine pack or completion of the placeholder workflow bridge.

Approval checks are descriptor-controlled and inspect an approved request field; do not describe them as authenticated human authorization or an automatic ban on every mutating tool. Trace persistence is implemented, not a demonstrated tamper-proof audit service.
